assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Four @TableTest methods: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress, splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability, choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount, keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable
assertions.evidence: Expected outputs vary per row and are derived transformations (e.g. 'W1:[camera,lens]' vs input '[camera, lens]'), not fixed or verbatim copies

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone
assertions.evidence: @Description states the fewest-shipments and companion tie-breaker rules; e.g. 'the fewest-shipments combination must be chosen even when it means overriding a warehouse that only partially covers the order.'

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: Availability table has 6 rows including both 'In-stock item not held for a backordered item' and 'In-stock item not held for a pre-ordered item', redundantly covering the same obligation (b), and fulfillment/address table has 6 rows including two interaction rows ('Items sharing an address group together...' and 'Delivery split by address, plus a separate pickup item') beyond the single optional interaction case.

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented in a @TableTest
assertions.evidence: 'Delivery and pickup items always split | ["camera:DELIVERY:Addr-A", "mug:PICKUP:"] | [camera, mug]'

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented in a @TableTest
assertions.evidence: 'Same type, different delivery addresses | ["camera:DELIVERY:Addr-A", "watch:DELIVERY:Addr-B"] | [camera, watch]'

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation is represented as its own @TableTest

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest

assertions.text: Compound output expressed as native TableTest list/map/set, not hand-rolled string
